limits: The GitHub Actions App ID is not a workflow-specific publisher identity.
Workflow/job permissions can request GITHUB_TOKEN authority; read-only defaults alone do not reserve tag creation for one workflow or environment.
A protected environment constrains refs and credential availability, not an arbitrary workflow by itself. Protected control-plane policy and actual nonpublisher denial evidence are also required.
No installation identity, credentials, environment/ref policy or npm trusted-publisher registration has been enrolled or qualified by this work.

proposedBoundary.npmAuthentication: short-lived OIDC through the existing trusted publisher, with exact workflow/environment registration readback
proposedBoundary.githubAuthentication: separately authorized repository-only GitHub App if built-in token isolation cannot be proven
proposedBoundary.canonicalInstalledCliVerification: separate read-only job without publisher environment, OIDC or installation-token authority

requiredBeforeActivation: Explicit owner authorization for any repository-only App or credential enrollment.
Independently read back the actual GitHub App ID, installation repository scope and exact minimal permissions; do not confuse installation ID with App ID.
Read back zero-reviewer environment/ref constraints and npm workflow/environment trusted-publisher binding.
Prove qualified main publication and denial for fork, arbitrary-ref and nonpublisher paths without real package publication unless separately authorized.
Prove creation-only tag authority independently from no-bypass movement/deletion controls.
Coordinate follow-on jobs explicitly; do not depend on GITHUB_TOKEN-created tag events, and prevent duplicate publication when other token types do trigger events.
